title: On kindness and empathy, in members' own words · AquaTerra
description: Essays by AquaTerra members on judging less, saying no, being thanked, speaking up and finding happiness. Read the pieces, then see kindness in action.
lede: On kindness and empathy gathers essays by AquaTerra members about how we treat each other: judging people too fast, saying no without guilt, being taken for granted, and speaking up when no one seems to listen. Read them as a set of small arguments for paying attention.

sections.heading: stop before you judge
body: Before You Judge Read This asks what would change if we stopped to consider the full story before we rushed to judge. It begins with a cab ride across the city, nothing dramatic, and turns that small moment into a question about how quickly we decide what someone is like.

Voicing One's Opinions opens with a question most people know: have you hesitated to speak your mind, not because you feared being wrong, but because you were not sure anyone would listen? The essay is about that hesitation, and about the people who get ignored when they do speak up.

sections.heading: saying no, and being thanked
body: The Quiet Power of Saying No starts from the lesson most of us grow up with, that yes opens doors, and asks what changes when you stop saying yes to everything. Cross It Anyway takes the line about crossing oceans for people who would not cross a puddle for you, and asks whether the choice is really about them or about who you are.

Ungrateful Much is blunt about people who take your time, kindness and support and offer no thanks. It's Just a Joke looks at the excuse we hear when a comment has gone too far, and at how it leaves people feeling uncertain or small.

sections.heading: feelings in a loud world
body: Lost in the Noise says everything feels loud right now, with notifications, opinions and expectations, and that the writer has started losing track of what they believe. Chasing Happiness argues that we treat happiness as a reward we will get once we achieve enough, change enough or become enough.

Dynamics is about how the same person gets very different reactions in different rooms, sometimes at the centre of attention and sometimes like an ant on the floor. Empathy becomes action in the drives: [Smile Notes](/impact/smile-notes), a kindness campaign where volunteers hand out affirmation notes and toffees, has {count:smile-notes} drives, and [volunteering for teenagers](/impact/volunteering-for-teens-in-kolkata) covers how teens take part.

learnings: Stopping to hear the full story before judging is one of the ideas these essays return to.
Saying no can be a quiet kind of power rather than a failure of kindness.
Kindness that is never thanked can leave a person drained, and the essays say so openly.
Hesitating to speak up is common enough to be a theme of its own, and it is worth naming.

faqs.q: What do AquaTerra's members write about kindness and empathy?
faqs.a: They write about judging people too quickly, saying no without guilt, being taken for granted, the jokes that make people feel small, and the noise that makes it hard to know what you believe.

faqs.q: Why does empathy matter for a volunteer?
faqs.a: Empathy is the habit of hearing the full story before acting, and it shapes how a volunteer talks to the children and neighbours at a drive.
Yes. Smile Notes is a kindness campaign in which volunteers hand out affirmation notes and a toffee to passersby, and AquaTerra has run {count:smile-notes} Smile Notes drives.

faqs.q: Are these essays written by AquaTerra members?
faqs.a: Yes. They are written by AquaTerra members, in their own words, and published on the site.

faqs.q: Where can I see kindness turned into action?
faqs.a: The page on volunteering for teenagers and the page on student leadership show how these ideas become drives in Kolkata, run by teams who plan, run and write up their own work.
